body:
After hearing so much about these films thanks to their monumental box office success in China, I needed to see them for myself because I think it's pretty nice to see international animation achieve something like this and I would like to support more of that. So what are my first thoughts on this first film? Well, it's complicated.

It's a little frustrating because the good stuff in "Ne Zha" is really good, especially in the action department where it really impressed me. The action sequences here are not only inspired and creative, but they're also beautifully orchestrated and animated with some gorgeous movement and colors, creating an epic atmosphere that is super entertaining to watch. They are so good that it reminded me of the quality of action in the first two "Kung Fu Panda" films, and I would even say that it is almost on the same level of those, which is a great compliment coming from me who's a big fan of those. Another very positive point is the story, which is really interesting and that despite the problems I'll mention in a moment, managed to hold my attention and get me invested when things got more serious. I really liked Ne Zha as a character, he's the type of protagonist that could have easily been annoying and hard to relate to, but they did a good job of making him charismatic and with a compelling emotional arc that makes it easy to feel for him. All of these things make me want to praise the film more than I actually will because these are very good elements, but unfortunately they are dragged down by its issues.

The worst of them is by far the juvenile and childish humor, which is not only not funny but also embarrassing because of how low it gets at times, and to make matters worse, it ends up really messing up the dramatic tone that the story tries to build. I also hated Taiyi's character, he's a forced addition for bad comic relief and the film didn't need that, and if he's part of Chinese legend then the choices they made with him just didn't work for me at all. Another problem is that despite a solid story that ends up working due to the strength of its merits, the script could've used a rewrite because many plot points are advanced too quickly and abruptly, particularly Ne Zha's friendship with Aobing. I hate to have such mixed thoughts about a movie that has so many good things in it, but that's just the way it is sometimes. Overall I recommend checking it out because there are moments here that I really liked and are worth the price of admission, but keep your expectations under control. And hey, if the things that bothered me don't bother you, then in that case you'll like it even more than I did.

I'll definitely check out "Ne Zha 2" whenever I can and I hope it's an improvement.

This was epic animation at it's best. A tale of overcoming prejudice, finding unusual friendship and deciding your own fate. My eyes have never watered up watching animation but this one did it.....yeah it's that's good. It's Feb of 2020 and this has been by far the best film I have downloaded and watched since the year has come in. Do I recommend? Hell to yes! A story that clearly defines the meaning of not to judge a book by it's cover. A story we all can relate to.

Very exotic while the aesthetic definitely wouldn't turn western audience off. Great animation, you can tell the budget is substantial, I would say that the production value is at least on par with Pixar. Surprisingly good film.

The Nezha animated movie has several standout aspects, with its top-notch animation being the biggest plus. However, the pacing of the movie is somewhat slow. On the other hand, the climax is exceptionally well-done, with a thrilling transition from the pre-climax. The music is average and lacks impact. Nevertheless, there are a few memorable dialogues in the climax that leave a lasting impression.

PLOT :: The Primus extracts a Mixed Yuan Bead into a Spirit Seed and a Demon Pill. The Spirit Seed can be reincarnated as a human to help King Zhou establish a new dynasty, whereas the Demon Pill will create a devil threatening humanity. Ne Zha is the one who is destined to be the hero, but instead he becomes a devil incarnate, because the Spirit Seed and a Demon Pill are switched.

There have been over 10 years since I go to the theater watching the Chinese garbage movies. This one really really changed my mind. I see a glimpse of light of the Chinese animation movies, and a fire for the whole Chinese movie industry.
